svg.aria-label: Week 11 managed Prometheus. A self-managed Prometheus runs on an Ubuntu virtual machine in sub-lab-dev, with no inbound port open and a public IP used only for egress. A user-assigned managed identity is attached to the virtual machine, so Prometheus obtains a token from the instance metadata service and holds no credential of its own. Prometheus remote-writes over HTTPS to the metrics ingestion endpoint of the data collection rule that the Azure Monitor workspace creates for itself. The identity holds Monitoring Metrics Publisher on that data collection rule and nothing wider, a grant that takes about thirty minutes to take effect, during which writes are refused with HTTP 403. The Azure Monitor workspace stores Prometheus time series, is queried with PromQL, and retains data for eighteen months at no storage cost. An Azure Managed Grafana instance reads the workspace through its own system-assigned identity holding Monitoring Data Reader. A Prometheus rule group deployed by Terraform evaluates one recording rule and one alert rule against the workspace, with no Kubernetes cluster named anywhere.
svg.text: No cluster anywhere. A Prometheus on a VM, writing to Azure with no secret.

attached to the VM, so Prometheus asks the
instance metadata service for a token

its metrics ingestion endpoint is what accepts the write
the identity holds Monitoring Metrics Publisher here —
on the rule, not the workspace, not the subscription
~30 MINUTES to take effect. Until then: HTTP 403
Azure Monitor workspace
NOT a Log Analytics workspace. Prometheus time series,

Managed Grafana
Standard — the only SKU
azurerm can express
reads via its own identity
Prometheus rule group
1 recording rule
1 alert rule
clusterName: empty
The grant is the week's trap. Monitoring Metrics Publisher on the data collection rule takes roughly thirty minutes to
propagate — six times the same role in week 08. The apply finishes long before the pipeline works, and an empty query
in between is indistinguishable from a broken one. So the validation polls rather than asking once.
Managed Prometheus SCRAPES only AKS and Arc-enabled Kubernetes. remote_write accepts a VM, which is why there is no
cluster here — and why the rule group's clusterName is empty while its scope is the workspace itself.
